title: To Lower Case
description:
# To Lower Case

Given a string `s`, return *the string after replacing every uppercase letter with the same lowercase letter*.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "Hello"
**Output:** "hello"

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "here"
**Output:** "here"

## Example 3:

**Input:** s = "LOVELY"
**Output:** "lovely"

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 100`
*   `s` consists of printable ASCII characters.

solutions.name: Character Manipulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Convert the string to a character array. For each character, only values in the ASCII uppercase range `A` through `Z` are adjusted by the lowercase offset `('a' - 'A')`; every other printable ASCII character is copied unchanged.

## Key Insight

In ASCII, uppercase and lowercase English letters are separated by a fixed offset. The range guard is part of the algorithm because digits, spaces, and punctuation must not be shifted.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Bitwise OR Conversion
solutions.description:
## Approach

For characters in the ASCII uppercase range, set bit `0x20` with `current | 32`. This converts `A` through `Z` to `a` through `z`; characters outside the range are appended unchanged.

## Key Insight

The bit trick is only safe after the uppercase range check. Without that guard, symbols such as `[` and `]` would also be changed because they share the same bit position.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: StringBuilder Streaming Conversion
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build the answer from left to right with a `StringBuilder`. Convert each uppercase ASCII letter by offset arithmetic and append either the converted letter or the original character.

## Key Insight

This route avoids mutating a copied character array and makes the output construction explicit. It is useful when teaching how to stream-transform a string one character at a time.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Character API Conversion
solutions.description:
## Approach

Iterate through the string and append `Character.toLowerCase(current)` for every character. The Java character API leaves non-letter printable ASCII characters unchanged.

## Key Insight

This is the library-backed baseline. It teaches the production-safe primitive while still walking through the string so the cost and transformation are visible.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: ASCII Lookup Table
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a constant-size lookup table for ASCII characters. Initialize every character to map to itself, then overwrite `A` through `Z` with their lowercase partners and transform the input by table lookup.

## Key Insight

A table separates the classification work from the transformation pass. Because the input is printable ASCII, a 128-entry table is sufficient and independent of input length.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
